summary: Tennessee Division of Forestry lookout site on the Scott-Campbell line at 2,749 ft; the list marks it removed and only the base survives.

facts.status_note: The Tennessee list marks the tower removed. The Scott County encyclopedia says only the base of the tower survives.

events.note: The encyclopedia's general description of steel lookout towers says the cab was where a lookout was posted during fire season, with a telephone to fire wardens or crews. It does not say this tower had that cab. No year is given.
The encyclopedia says a Braden Mountain tower was removed and reassembled here, and that it no longer remains. No year is given.
The encyclopedia says gradual decommissioning ended active use of the installation. It dates the shift to planes and 911 calls to the mid-1970s, and gives no closing year for this site.
The Tennessee list marks the tower removed. No year is given.

evidence.supports: Summit on the Scott-Campbell county line in northeastern Tennessee
evidence.quote: View Tree Knob is a mountain summit located on the boundary between Scott and Campbell counties in northeastern Tennessee.
It stands at 2,750 feet in elevation

evidence.supports: Historically the site of a Tennessee Division of Forestry wildfire lookout tower; remnants at the summit
evidence.quote: It was historically the site of a Tennessee Division of Forestry wildfire lookout tower, remnants of which survive at the summit.

evidence.supports: Agency chose the site for its prominence and sightlines
evidence.quote: a choice driven directly by its prominence and unobstructed sightlines over the surrounding forested landscape

evidence.supports: General description of steel lookout towers, not specific to this tower: seven-foot by seven-foot cab where the lookout was stationed during fire season
evidence.quote: had a seven-foot by seven-foot cab at the top where the lookout was stationed during fire season

evidence.supports: Telephone in the cab to fire wardens or crews (same general description of steel towers, not specific to this tower)
evidence.quote: A telephone in the cab allowed the lookout to connect with fire wardens or fire crews.

evidence.supports: Braden Mountain tower removed and reassembled at View Tree Knob; no longer remains
evidence.quote: Of these, the Braden Mountain tower was removed and reassembled at View Tree Knob, though it no longer remains.

evidence.supports: List entry for Braden Mountain marked moved
From the mid-1970s, planes and 911 calls made the manned tower network obsolete
evidence.quote: Since the mid-1970s, forestry employees became more dependent on fire-spotting planes and fire reports from 911 emergency calls, rendering the manned tower network obsolete.

evidence.supports: Gradual decommissioning ended active use of the installation
evidence.quote: The gradual decommissioning of fire lookout infrastructure across the state brought an end to active use of the View Tree Knob installation.

evidence.supports: Only the base of the tower survives today
evidence.quote: Today, only the base of the View Tree Knob tower survives.

evidence.supports: Much of the surrounding landscape is in the North Cumberland Wildlife Management Area
evidence.quote: The North Cumberland Wildlife Management Area encompasses much of the surrounding landscape.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Tennessee list places the tower site in Campbell County. The encyclopedia puts the summit on the Scott-Campbell county line. The story reports both and does not pick one.

sources.title: TN lookout tower: CAT007 View Tree Knob

notes_for_editor: Brief status (gone), county (Campbell, per the list), and elevation (837.9 m, which matches 2,749 ft) agree with the list. No build year, design, height, or closing year for this tower appears in the sources reached, so the story leaves them out. The encyclopedia is a local reference rather than a primary record. Its Braden Mountain statement is not corroborated; the list marks Braden as moved but does not say where. Cross-check us-tn-braden-mountain against this. The encyclopedia's cab description is written about steel lookout towers in general, so it may not describe this tower's cab. Access is not stated in any source, so no access fact is recorded.
